div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1286px; height: 1px; padding-top: 923px; margin-left: 68px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;

div.div: Why sessions must be torn down: with long-lived sessions the PEP authenticates once per handshake. A revoked device would keep its open connection, and every request becomes a cache miss and a WAN round trip — turning a revoked device into load on the PDP. Revocation therefore closes sessions, and session lifetime is capped by the certificate TTL.
